rehearsal.reviewBody: Emil will not guess or touch a live portal.
rehearsal.approvedBody: The approved twin was executed in the sandbox and every action was attached to the run record.

edge.heading: Your core systems are connected.
edge.body: TMS, WMS, EDI, and internal AI can prepare the answer. When the next step lives behind a third-party portal, Emil operates that controlled final stretch.

comparison.label: Before Emil
comparison.title: The portal becomes someone's swivel chair.
comparison.body: Manual copying, fragmented screenshots, hidden exceptions, and no consistent rehearsal before submission.

comparison.label: With Emil
comparison.title: The portal becomes a controlled operating surface.
comparison.body: Approved data, mapped into a faithful twin, exceptions made visible, and irreversible action held for a person.

capabilities.title: Live portal twin
capabilities.body: See the mapped state before anything reaches production.

capabilities.title: Visible exceptions
capabilities.body: Ambiguity and mismatch are surfaced for judgment.

capabilities.title: Human checkpoints
capabilities.body: Irreversible action waits for accountable approval.

capabilities.title: Complete run record
capabilities.body: Inputs, decisions, responses, and artifacts stay together.

platform.heading: Keep your systems of record.
platform.accentHeading: Add an operator beyond the API.
platform.body: Emil complements the enterprise AI, integration, and logistics platforms you already trust. They decide and prepare. Emil turns that approved intent into controlled browser work where conventional connectivity ends.

points.title: Shows its work before action
points.body: A portal twin exposes every mapped field.

points.title: Returns the evidence
points.body: Responses, decisions, and artifacts travel back together.

process.heading: Act only after the whole path is visible.
process.body: Emil separates preparation from execution. A complete dry run makes the mapping, portal state, exceptions, and intended outcome inspectable before anything irreversible can happen.

steps.title: Scope
steps.body: Lock the portal, process, permissions, and success condition.

steps.title: Read
steps.body: Take only the approved shipment or booking record.

steps.title: Twin
steps.body: Build the portal state without touching production.

steps.title: Resolve
steps.body: Surface ambiguity, mismatch, and missing evidence.

steps.title: Approve
steps.body: Give the accountable operator a clear checkpoint.

steps.title: Execute & record
steps.body: Perform the approved simulation and return a full receipt.

process.failClosedTitle: The control is structural, not cosmetic.
process.failClosedBody: If the page changes, evidence conflicts, or the approved scope is exceeded, Emil stops.

workflows.kicker: Start where the friction is highest
workflows.heading: Two narrow wedges.
workflows.body: Begin with a repetitive portal process that has clear source data, human ownership, and a measurable outcome.

primary.title: Customs filing
primary.body: Carry an approved shipment record into a national single window, expose filing exceptions, pause for review, and return the rehearsal receipt.

primary.title: Third-party carrier booking
primary.body: Translate an approved TMS booking into a carrier portal, verify sailings and constraints, request approval, and return a confirmation.

more.title: Track-and-trace reconciliation
more.body: Compare portal events with internal milestones and route exceptions.

more.title: EDI gap filling
more.body: Complete portal-only steps when a message path is missing.

more.title: RFQ portals
more.body: Carry approved lane requests into tender and quote surfaces.

more.title: Proof-of-delivery retrieval
more.body: Find, verify, and return delivery evidence into the right record.

pilot.heading: Pilot one narrow process.
pilot.body: One portal. One country or site. One KPI. Enough control to prove the operating model without turning the pilot into a platform program.

steps.title: Baseline the manual path
steps.body: Volume, handling time, exception rate, and evidence quality.

steps.title: Rehearse with real rules
steps.body: In a safe twin using representative, non-production data.

steps.title: Prove one KPI
steps.body: Cycle time, touch time, error rate, or record completeness.

footer.tagline: Think in simulation. Act with precision.
